Cursor runs a credit-based pricing model (since June 2025): Hobby free / Pro $20 / Pro+ $60 / Ultra $200 / Teams $40/seat / Enterprise custom. Monthly credit pool equals plan price in dollars; depletes per-model: Pro's $20 yields ~225 Claude 3.5 Sonnet requests, ~500 GPT-4o requests, or ~550 Gemini requests. Direct comp for Vrooli subscription-as-gateway tier economics and token-pass-through markup math. Sources: https://costbench.com/software/ai-coding-assistants/cursor/ | https://www.vantage.sh/blog/cursor-pricing-explained | https://www.nxcode.io/resources/news/cursor-ai-pricing-plans-guide-2026. Source scan ids: as-1777062700091991558. For monetization market-validator consumption.

BYOK coding tools (Cline, Aider) run zero-subscription / zero-markup; Cline cites 5M VS Code installs on this model. Windsurf $15/mo positioned as 'best value' subscription tier. Third-party comparisons surface a decision-frame indie developers use: at >$40/mo API spend, a $20 subscription with credits beats BYOK; below $40/mo, BYOK wins. Implication for Vrooli subscription-as-gateway: must clear the same threshold — cheaper than BYOK summed across the scenarios a buyer would otherwise credential individually — or the framing must shift to 'convenience pays X/mo over raw cost' which monetization should evaluate explicitly. Sources: https://www.morphllm.com/ai-coding-agent | https://awesomeagents.ai/pricing/ai-coding-tools-pricing/. Source scan ids: as-1777062700091991559. For monetization market-validator consumption.
